candidate.educational_objective: Treat an EHR alert failure as a patient-safety signal requiring investigation, validation, monitoring, and improvement of clinical decision-support safeguards.

options.A: Investigate the clinical decision-support failure and continue systematic testing, monitoring, and improvement of EHR alerts and order-entry safeguards.
options.B: Disable all medication alerts permanently after this event because one missed warning shows that clinical decision support creates more risk than benefit.
options.C: Return immediately to paper-only ordering throughout the organization because an isolated EHR alert failure proves electronic ordering cannot be made safe.
options.D: Leave the system unchanged if no second failure occurs because clinical decision-support tools do not require ongoing monitoring after implementation.

candidate.rationale: ONC's 2025 SAFER CPOE with Decision Support guide identifies recommended safety practices for the design, implementation, use, and monitoring of orders, alerts, warnings and clinical decision support. ONC also emphasizes configuration, validation, maintenance, monitoring and improvement of health IT. A therefore addresses the failure as a safety signal requiring investigation and continued system improvement. B, C and D either abandon useful safeguards or ignore the need for ongoing monitoring.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Organizations should optimize the safety and safe use of EHR order entry/CDS through design, implementation, validation, use, monitoring and improvement of alerts, warnings and related safeguards.
